ab_louise_falls_area.blurb: A small cluster of six short routes on the quartzite walls beside the waterfall at the far end of Lake Louise, within the Back of the Lake zone in Banff National Park. Three are bolted sport lines and three are trad, with bolted anchors and pitches around 25 metres. The grades stay low, nearly all around 5.6 or easier, which makes it a handy spot for learning to lead and for guided beginner days. The harder climbing in the zone lies on other buttresses nearby. Expect a lakeside walk to get there rather than a roadside pullout.

ab_7_the_water_park.blurb: The Water Park is a compact group of six sport routes tucked into the Cloud Break strip of cliff on the Bow Valley side of Grotto Mountain, a short walk beyond the main Cloud Break wall, finishing up a small rock step. Grades cluster at the 5.10 level, with a single 5.9. The draw is the unusual rock: blue-tinted, water-worn walls with jugs and tufa-like features. It is a small, quiet-feeling sector rather than a big crag, best treated as an add-on to a Cloud Break day.

ab_healing_boulder.blurb: One of the larger single boulders at Frank Slide in the Crowsnest Pass, with problems on both its east and west faces. Six problems here range from easy V0 lines up to a couple of V5s, with a few V2 to V3 in between. Many are tall for bouldering, technical and arete-based, with crimpy sit starts. Bring pads and spotters, and watch for loose holds, since a block has come off one of the easy problems before. The boulder is near the road at the edge of town, so the walk is brief.

ab_icebox.blurb: The Icebox is the first and busiest cluster of boulders in the Skyline area of the Porcupine Hills, sometimes called the Upper Area, and it has the densest collection of blocks in the zone. Six problems are on record here, from V0 up to about V4, so it suits climbers working through the easy and middle grades. The stone is sandstone that is described as lovely but fragile, so keep off it when it is damp. It sits out in open grassland country and gets the most traffic of any Skyline sector.

ab_moonlight_snowline_area.blurb: The main climbing zone of Evan-Thomas Creek in Kananaskis, a winter ice area with six routes. Two classic two-pitch flows, Moonlight on the left and Snowline on the right, are the headline lines, and the remaining routes include a few easier ice climbs and one short mixed line. Most of the ice is moderate, with the two big flows at the harder end of the range. Reaching it takes a long walk up the frozen creek, over an hour, though the creek area is described as having no avalanche hazard.

ab_the_golf_course.blurb: A juggy slab of good rock at Grassi Lakes above Canmore, with six bolted sport routes between Roadhouse and Meathooks. These are the gentlest climbs at Grassi: three at 5.5, two at 5.6 and a single 5.7. That makes it a favourite for first-timers, families and groups with children, and it can get crowded. Some routes work well for top-roping. Wear a helmet, as loose rock can come down from above. The walk is either a half-hour past the lakes or shorter from the higher lot.

ab_school_of_rock.blurb: A short wall in Cougar Canyon above Canmore, technically an extension of the House of Cards cliff and the first one you meet on the left walking in, about ten to twenty minutes up the canyon. Six bolted sport routes run from 5.8 to the low 5.11s, with two at 5.10 and two at 5.11. The lines are short and cruxy, some of them bouldery, and the first bolts are high, so carry a stick clip. Because it is easy to walk past, check you are at the right wall.
